record.paper_title: QM2017: Status and Key open Questions in Ultra-Relativistic Heavy-Ion Physics
record.original_question: Can out-of-equilibrium remnants and particle-specific freeze-out hierarchies be identified and measured well enough to reconstruct the dynamics of hadronisation, including how different reaction channels and hadronic cross sections cause different particle species to freeze out at different times and temperatures?

evidence.quote: If equilibrium is the problem, hiding dynamics, looking for out-of-equilibrium remnants may be the solution to uncover dynamics.

Therefore, given the large variety of reaction channels and hadronic cross sections, it is not a question of if different particles will freeze-out at different times and temperatures, but only a question of how big the effect is in each individual case.
Identifying such a freeze-out hierarchy in certain particle ratios could make, not break, the case for hadro-chemistry!

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the late stages of an ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collision, in which a hot, dense fireball of strongly-interacting matter expands and cools, producing hadrons that are eventually detected. Two notions of decoupling are usually distinguished:

(i) Chemical freeze-out, the space-time hypersurface on which inelastic (number-changing) reactions cease, fixing the relative abundances (yields) of each hadron species.
(ii) Kinetic (thermal) freeze-out, the hypersurface on which elastic (momentum-changing) reactions cease, fixing the transverse-momentum spectra of each species.

Because different hadron species (e.g. pions, kaons, protons, multistrange baryons such as Ξ and Ω, light nuclei, charm hadrons) couple to the hadronic medium through reaction channels with very different cross sections, each species is expected in principle to freeze out on its own hypersurface, characterised by its own decoupling temperature T_i and time τ_i. Denote by 𝓗 = {(T_i, τ_i)}_i this particle-specific freeze-out hierarchy, and by 𝓡 the set of out-of-equilibrium remnants — deviations of yields, ratios, and momentum distributions from the predictions of a single global equilibrium freeze-out — that encode the underlying hadronisation dynamics.

Problem. Determine whether suitably chosen observables (in particular ratios of identified-particle yields, transverse-momentum spectra, fluctuations, and correlations of the species above) can be measured with sufficient precision and theoretically modelled with sufficient control to:

(a) detect statistically significant species-dependent differences (T_i, τ_i) ≠ (T_j, τ_j), thereby establishing the hierarchy 𝓗;

(b) extract from 𝓡 the dynamical information about reaction channels and hadronic cross sections that drives this hierarchy;

(c) thereby reconstruct the dynamics of hadronisation — that is, the time-ordered sequence of decouplings and the role of specific hadronic interactions — rather than only its time-integrated, equilibrium-averaged outcome.

Provide a quantitative framework (observables, estimators, and uncertainty budget) capable of carrying out (a)–(c), or prove an obstruction showing that hadronisation dynamics cannot be reconstructed in this way from currently accessible observables.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent literature has established partial evidence for a particle-specific freeze-out hierarchy: mass-dependent kinetic freeze-out and flavor-dependent (strange vs. non-strange) chemical freeze-out have been extracted from yield and pT-spectrum analyses at AGS/SPS/RHIC/LHC energies, and multiple-freeze-out (e.g. separate strange) scenarios are widely discussed. However, fully reconstructing hadronisation dynamics — including disentangling cross-section-driven channel-by-channel decoupling times and out-of-equilibrium remnants in a model-independent way — remains an active, unresolved program.

status_evidence.title: Hierarchy of kinetic freeze-out parameters in low energy heavy-ion collisions
status_evidence.snippet: Clear existence of a mass dependent hierarchy in thermal freeze-out of hadrons; heavier hadrons decouple earlier as the fireball cools.
status_evidence.claim: Mass-dependent kinetic freeze-out hierarchy has been measured, partially establishing 𝓗.

status_evidence.title: Systematics of chemical freeze-out parameters in heavy-ion collision experiments
status_evidence.snippet: Strange hadrons fix their chemical composition earlier than non-strange light hadrons due to smaller inelastic cross-sections; nonstrange freeze-out temperature is consistently lower than the strange one.
status_evidence.claim: Flavor-dependent chemical freeze-out is supported by data, providing partial evidence for the hierarchy linked to reaction cross sections.

status_evidence.title: Freeze-out and thermalization in relativistic heavy ion collisions
status_evidence.snippet: Freeze-out is a complicated process involving duration in time and a hierarchy where different types of particles and reactions switch-off at different times.
status_evidence.claim: The dynamical reconstruction of hadronisation through freeze-out hierarchy remains an active research area.
